61148-hiwa-a-tale-of-ancient-hawaii.title: Hiwa A Tale Of Ancient Hawaii
61148-hiwa-a-tale-of-ancient-hawaii.creator: Unknown
61148-hiwa-a-tale-of-ancient-hawaii.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. the Waipio River, cold from the mountain-side, clear and sparkling, fell six hundred feet to a narrow shelf of rock, and then, dropping a thousand feet more at a single plunge, suddenly became a sluggish stream, with a current hardly perceptible, winding its tortuous way to the sea.

arxiv-1801-01337.title: Edge-based compartmental modelling of an SIR epidemic on a dual-layer static-dynamic multiplex network with tunable clustering
arxiv-1801-01337.creator: Rosanna C Barnard, Istvan Z Kiss, Luc Berthouze, Joel C Miller
arxiv-1801-01337.description: Abstract The duration, type and structure of connections between individuals in real-world populations play a crucial role in how diseases invade and spread. Here, we incorporate the aforementioned heterogeneities into a model by considering a dual-layer static-dynamic multiplex network. The static network layer affords tunable clustering and describes an individual’s permanent community structure.

arxiv-2110-06837.title: Effect of damped oscillations in the inflationary potential
arxiv-2110-06837.creator: Akhil Antony, Shweta Jain
arxiv-2110-06837.description: Abstract We investigate the effect of damped oscillations on a nearly flat inflationary potential and the features they produce in the power-spectrum and bi-spectrum. We compare the model with the Planck data using Plik unbinned and CamSpec clean likelihood and we are able to obtain noticeable improvement in fit compared to the power-law Λ \Lambda CDM model.

arxiv-2203-01127.title: GCOS - The Global Cosmic Ray Observatory
arxiv-2203-01127.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by *. Nature is providing particles with energies exceeding 100 EeV. Their existence imposes immediate questions: Are they ordinary particles, accelerated in extreme astrophysical environments, or are they annihilation or decay products of super-heavy dark matter or other exotic objects? If the particles are accelerated in extreme astrophysical environments, are their sources related to those of high-energy neutrinos, gamma rays, and/or gravitational waves, such as the recently observed mergers of compact objects?

arxiv-2302-11496.title: Ultra-high resolution observations of plasmoid-mediated magnetic reconnection in the deep solar atmosphere
arxiv-2302-11496.creator: Luc H. M. Rouppe van der Voort, Michiel van Noort, Jaime de la Cruz Rodríguez
arxiv-2302-11496.description: Abstract Context. Magnetic reconnection in the deep solar atmosphere can give rise to enhanced emission in the Balmer hydrogen lines, a phenomenon referred to as Ellerman bombs. Aims. To effectively trace magnetic reconnection below the canopy of chromospheric fibrils, we analyzed unique spectroscopic observations of Ellerman bombs in the H α \alpha line. Methods.

arxiv-2308-12734.title: Real-time Detection of AI-Generated Speech for DeepFake Voice Conversion
arxiv-2308-12734.creator: Jordan J. Bird, Ahmad Lotfi
arxiv-2308-12734.description: Abstract There are growing implications surrounding generative AI in the speech domain that enable voice cloning and real-time voice conversion from one individual to another. This technology poses a significant ethical threat and could lead to breaches of privacy and misrepresentation, thus there is an urgent need for real-time detection of AI-generated speech for DeepFake Voice Conversion.

arxiv-2311-07932.title: Cross-subject dual-domain fusion network with task-related and task-discriminant component analysis enhancing one-shot SSVEP classification
arxiv-2311-07932.creator: Yang Deng, Zhiwei Ji, Yijun Wang, and S.Kevin Zhou
arxiv-2311-07932.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yang Deng, Zhiwei Ji, Yijun Wang, and S.Kevin Zhou. This study addresses the significant challenge of developing efficient decoding algorithms for classifying steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) in scenarios characterized by extreme scarcity of calibration data, where only one calibration is available for each stimulus target. To tackle this problem, we introduce a novel cross-subject dual-domain fusion network (CSDuDoFN) incorporating task-related and task-discriminant component analysis (TRCA and TDCA) for one-shot SSVEP classification.

arxiv-2311-14082.title: Geometric Covering using Random Fields
arxiv-2311-14082.creator: Felipe Gonçalves, Daniel Keren, Amit Shahar, Gal Yehuda
arxiv-2311-14082.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Felipe Gonçalves, Daniel Keren, Amit Shahar, Gal Yehuda. A set of vectors S ⊆ ℝ d S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d} is ( k 1 , ε ) (k_{1},\varepsilon) -clusterable if there are k 1 k_{1} balls of radius ε \varepsilon that cover S S .

arxiv-2406-00541.title: Bishop-like theorems for non-subnormal operators Thanks: The research of the first and third authors was supported by the National Science Center (NCN) Grant OPUS No. DEC-2021/43/B/ST1/01651. The research of the second author was supported by Basic Science Research Program through the National Resea
arxiv-2406-00541.creator: Zenon Jan Jabłoński, Il Bong Jung, Jan Stochel
arxiv-2406-00541.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zenon Jan Jabłoński, Il Bong Jung, Jan Stochel. The celebrated Bishop theorem states that an operator is subnormal if and only if it is the strong limit of a net (or a sequence) of normal operators. By the Agler-Stankus theorem, 2 2 -isometries behave similarly to subnormal operator in the sense that the role of subnormal operators is played by 2 2 -isometries, while the role of normal operators is played by Brownian unitaries.

arxiv-2502-13759.title: Geolocation with Real Human Gameplay Data: A Large-Scale Dataset and Human-Like Reasoning Framework
arxiv-2502-13759.creator: Zirui Song, Jingpu Yang, Yuan Huang, Jonathan Tonglet, Zeyu Zhang, Tao Cheng, Meng Fang, Iryna Gurevych, Xiuying Chen
arxiv-2502-13759.description: Abstract Geolocation aims to identify an image’s location and requires complex reasoning, playing an important role in navigation, monitoring, and cultural preservation. However, existing methods often yield coarse and non-interpretable predictions. A key challenge is the limited quality and scale of current geolocation datasets, which are typically small, automatically constructed, and suffer from noise and inconsistent difficulty.

arxiv-2510-17545.title: TrajMamba: An Efficient and Semantic-rich Vehicle Trajectory Pre-training Model
arxiv-2510-17545.creator: Yichen Liu, Yan Lin, Shengnan Guo, Zeyu Zhou, Youfang Lin, Huaiyu Wan
arxiv-2510-17545.description: Abstract Vehicle GPS trajectories record how vehicles move over time, storing valuable travel semantics, including movement patterns and travel purposes. Learning travel semantics effectively and efficiently is crucial for real-world applications of trajectory data, which is hindered by two major challenges. First, travel purposes are tied to the functions of the roads and points-of-interest (POIs) involved in a trip.

Whether oseltamivir absorption is adequate in severe influenza is unknown. We measured the steady state, plasma concentrations of nasogastrically administered os

pmc-11434981.title: Fish Consumption and DHA Supplementation during Pregnancy: Study of Gestational and Neonatal Outcomes
pmc-11434981.creator: Paola Gualtieri, Giulia Frank, Rossella Cianci, Francesca Dominici, Ilenia Mappa, Giuseppe Rizzo, Gemma Lou De Santis, Giulia Bigioni, Laura Di Renzo, Ann Anderson Berry
pmc-11434981.description: Several studies have explored the association between fish consumption during pregnancy and favorable neonatal outcomes, although some yield conflicting results. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends two to three servings of low-mercury fish per week for pregnant or breastfeeding women. However, fish can be a source of pollutants, like methylmercury, impacting neurological development.

pmc-11484120.title: Acetylcysteine synergizes PD-1 blockers against colorectal cancer progression by promoting TCF1+PD1+CD8+ T cell differentiation
pmc-11484120.creator: Wenchang Zhou, Mengdi Qu, Ying Yue, Ziwen Zhong, Ke Nan, Xingfeng Sun, Qichao Wu, Jie Zhang, Wankun Chen, Changhong Miao
pmc-11484120.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundProgrammed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade is essential in treating progressive colorectal cancer (CRC). However, some patients with CRC do not respond well to immunotherapy, possibly due to the exhaustion of CD8+ T cells in the tumor microenvironment. N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) can reduce CD8+ T cell exhaustion in vitro and induce their differentiation into long-lasting phenotypes, thus enhancing the anti-tumor effect of adoptive T cell transfer.

pmc-12382090.title: Predictive role of the muscle quality index for testosterone deficiency in adult males based on interpretable machine learning methods
pmc-12382090.creator: Lisheng Yu, Shunshun Cao, Botian Song, Yangyang Hu
pmc-12382090.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTestosterone deficiency (TD) is a clinically significant condition strongly associated with aging and metabolic syndrome. While previous studies have established links between muscle mass and TD, evidence regarding the relationship between muscle quality index (MQI) and TD remains limited.

pmc-12450896.title: Exploring AI tool adoption in higher education: evidence from a PLS-SEM model integrating multimodal literacy, self-efficacy, and university support
pmc-12450896.creator: Zixuan Zhao, Qi An, Jiaqi Liu
pmc-12450896.description: IntroductionFramed within the technology acceptance model, this study examines how multimodal literacy, self-efficacy, and university support affect students’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence tools and the students’ intentions to adopt them.MethodsSurvey data from 498 students were analyzed using PLS-SEM 4.0 and SPSS 29.

pmc-12489241.title: Exploring Bridge-Enhanced ACL Repair (BEAR) As a Novel Approach in Managing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Tear and Its Applicability in Indonesia
pmc-12489241.creator: Rio Taruna Jati, Aris Handoko, Bany Faris Amin
pmc-12489241.description: Objectives:Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears are prevalent among athletes, often considered a career-ending injury. Evolving management strategies seek to optimize outcomes while minimizing risks associated with repair and reconstruction. Bridge-enhanced ACL repair (BEAR) offers a novel approach using a scaffold implant to bridge and fuse torn ACL ends, aiming to restore the ligament’s original structure and function.

pmc-12589563.title: Secondary structure transitions and dual PIP2 binding define cardiac KCNQ1-KCNE1 channel gating
pmc-12589563.creator: Ling Zhong, Xiaoqing Lin, Xinyu Cheng, Shuangyan Wan, Yaoguang Hua, Weiwei Nan, Bin Hu, Xiangjun Peng, Zihan Zhou, Qiansen Zhang, Huaiyu Yang, Frank Noé, Zhenzhen Yan, Dexiang Jiang, Hangyu Zhang, Fengjiao Liu, Chenxin Xiao, Zhuo Zhou, Yimin Mou, Haijie Yu, Lijuan Ma, Chen Huang, Vincent Kam Wai Won
pmc-12589563.description: The KCNQ1 + KCNE1 potassium channel complex produces the slow delayed rectifier current (IKs) critical for cardiac repolarization. Loss-of-function mutations in KCNQ1 and KCNE1 cause long QT syndrome (LQTS) types 1 and 5 (LQT1/LQT5), accounting for over one-third of clinical LQTS cases.

pmc-12717935.title: Permittivity-asymmetric qBIC metasurfaces for refractive index sensing
pmc-12717935.creator: Xingye Yang, Alexander Antonov, Haiyang Hu, Andreas Tittl
pmc-12717935.description: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) provide exceptional light confinement due to their inherent decoupling from radiative channels. Small symmetry breaking transforms BIC into quasi-BIC (qBIC) that couples to free-space radiation enabling ultra-high-quality-factor (Q-factor) resonances desirable for refractive index (RI) sensing. In practical implementations, geometric asymmetry is typically employed.

pmc-13078855.title: Natural selection and recombination interact to structure genome‐wide variation in pines
pmc-13078855.creator: Chen‐Jui Yang, Tomas Funda, Rajiv Chaudhary, Zhi‐Qiang Chen, Maximiliano Estravis Barcala, Harry Wu
pmc-13078855.description: SUMMARYGenetic differentiation among populations often varies significantly across the genome due to factors such as selection and recombination, resulting in a heterogeneous genomic landscape. However, variation in low‐differentiation regions—genomic valleys—remains poorly understood. Moreover, most insights into plant genomic landscapes come from flowering plants, while comparable genome‐wide studies in other taxa, such as conifers, remain limited.

pmc-13346994.title: A nature-inspired osprey optimization based feature selection framework with stacking ensemble model for imbalance-aware credit card fraud detection
pmc-13346994.creator: Bharat Kumar Padhi, Bighnaraj Naik, Rajat Kumar Sahu, Rohit Kumar, Debahuti Mishra
pmc-13346994.description: Credit card fraud detection has emerged as a critical issue because of the extremely skewed data of transactions and the existence of redundant or non-critical features that influence model performance. This paper presents an ideal feature selection model, which was developed around the Feature Selection using Osprey Optimization Algorithm, a nature based optimization algorithm, and a stacking ensemble classifier.

pmc-13380761.title: Temporal variability in outcomes of identical regimens across newly diagnosed myeloma trials: a systematic review
pmc-13380761.creator: Ghulam Rehman Mohyuddin, Hector A Vaquera-Alfaro, Amandeep Godara, Aaron Goodman, Maria Mainou, Rajshekhar Chakraborty, Hadas Ditzian Kugler, Tomer Meirson
pmc-13380761.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundCross-trial comparisons in oncology are inherently problematic yet commonly performed. Diagnostic changes in 2014 have led to the inclusion of patients previously with smoldering myeloma being reclassified as having myeloma. Informative censoring may also affect results.

pmc-13547674.title: Comparable 2-year functional outcomes following vertebroplasty for thoracic and lumbar osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13547674.creator: Yong Ng, Jeremy Tze En Lim, Lei Jiang, Yee Gen Lim, Zhixing Marcus Ling, Chee Cheong Reuben Soh, Christian Hwee Yee Heng
pmc-13547674.description: Study Design Retrospective cohort study.Purpose To compare short- and medium-term patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) between thoracic and lumbar percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) cohorts for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs).Overview of Literature PVP is well-established for pain relief in OVCF; however, whether clinical outcomes vary by the anatomical location of the treated vertebrae, remains unclear.

pmc-13647558.title: Robot-assisted ureteral reconstruction combined with trans-trocar flexible ureteroscopy using a flexible and navigable suction ureteral access sheath: a case report and technical note
pmc-13647558.creator: Chaoyue Ji, Jianxing Li, Weiguo Hu, Gang Zhang
pmc-13647558.description: BackgroundSimultaneous management of upper urinary tract stricture and renal calculi remains a technical challenge in minimally invasive urology. Conventional hybrid techniques combining robotic reconstruction with standard flexible ureteroscopy often face limitations such as impaired visualization, irrigation fluid leakage, and difficulty in managing a substantial stone burden.
